what: HIGH (code audit CA-A04): the monitor's dry_run short-circuit on every exchange-side management call can never fire. order_monitor._build_account_client (order_monitor.py:1722) sets cfg['mode'] = getattr(acc, 'mode', 'live') or 'live', but TradingAccount has no .mode attribute -- the resolved state lives in acc.dry_run. MEASURED with the real config: all 11 accounts print hasattr(mode)=False and resolve to 'live', including ib_live (dry_run=True, real money, 'no socket opened, no orders placed') and oanda_practice (dry_run=True). So _send_close_to_exchange (:1804), _send_partial_close_to_exchange (:1938), _capture_fill_details (:1999) and _send_modify_to_exchange (:2078) would build a real client and send close/modify orders for any open trade row on a mode: dry_run account. Not firing today: 0 open rows on dry_run accounts among the last 1000 trades, and ib_live has an empty roster. It fires the moment a live account holding positions is demoted to dry_run (the Gate-2 demotion shape). Tests miss it because they use MagicMock accounts (which fabricate .mode) or patch _build_account_client. FIX (Tier-2, order path): 'mode': 'dry_run' if acc.dry_run else 'live', plus the real-TradingAccount test. Found by a CA-A04 reader sub-agent; re-verified by the lane.
